about.title: Foster City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Foster City is small — about 33,477 people living between SR-92 and the bay. When someone dies here in a preventable way, the loss ripples through a tight community. In 2025, the city recorded 107 injury collisions and 2 traffic deaths, with the heaviest collision counts along SR-92, Foster City Boulevard, and E Hillsdale Boulevard. To the families involved, those numbers are everything. A California wrongful death claim is a civil action, separate from any criminal charges or citations. It exists so that a spouse or domestic partner, children, and in some cases other dependents or heirs can seek compensation for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death; if a public agency in San Mateo County is involved, the window is much shorter. LawProactive is free to use. We connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so you can focus on your family.

whyChoose.title: Why Foster City Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can tell you plainly whether you qualify before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing limit is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency carry a much shorter clock. Getting connected soon keeps those doors open.

items.title: A civil path, apart from any criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not prosecutors act, your family can pursue funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance through a separate civil claim — on a contingency basis, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on SR-92 in Foster City. Does the criminal investigation affect our claim?
items.answer: Not directly. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal case, so you do not have to wait for charges or a conviction. Investigation records, including the collision report, often become useful evidence. An attorney can help you request them and preserve what matters.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California gives first priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children. If there are none, certain dependents and other heirs may have standing. Because the rules are specific, most families find it worth a free conversation with an attorney to confirm who should be named.

items.question: How long do we have, and what if a government vehicle was involved?
items.answer: Generally, two years from the date of death. If a public entity — for example a San Mateo County or state-operated vehicle or a road maintained by a public agency — played a role, a formal claim usually must be presented within months, not years. Acting sooner protects your choices.
